The central-peripheral neural axis and local breast innervation in regulating breast cancer

Mechanisms of the central-peripheral neural axis and local breast innervation in regulating breast cancer. A Sympathetic nerves release norepinephrine (NE), which binds to β-adrenergic receptors (β-AR) on CD8⁺T cells to activate the cAMP/PKA/CREB pathway, inhibiting CD8⁺T cells infiltration; NE also promotes VEGF expression in endothelial cells, enhancing angiogenesis and breast cancer cell proliferation. B Vagus nerve-derived acetylcholine (ACh) activates α7nAChR on TAMs, suppressing the NF-κB pathway to reduce IL-6/IL-1β secretion and promote M2 polarization; cytokines from immune cells reciprocally regulate neural activity. C Sensory nerve-secreted substance P (SP) binds to TACR1 on breast cancer cells, inducing partial cell death and single-stranded RNA release, which activates pro-metastatic genes in surviving cells. D Sensory nerve-derived CGRP binds to endothelial cell receptors to promote proliferation/migration (facilitating angiogenesis) and increases vascular permeability via VE-cadherin phosphorylation, enabling breast cancer cell intravasation and metastasis
